facts.statement: Utatsusaurus is the earliest known ichthyopterygian, living during the Early Triassic period approximately 245 to 250 million years ago.
facts.quote: Utatsusaurus hataii is the earliest-known ichthyopterygian which lived in the Early Triassic period (c. 245–250 million years ago).

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had a slender body and measured nearly 2.5 to 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was nearly 2.5 - 3 m long with a slender body.

facts.statement: The first specimen of Utatsusaurus was discovered in Utatsu-cho, now part of Minamisanriku-cho, in Miyagi Prefecture, Japan.
facts.quote: The first specimen was found in Utatsu-cho (now part of Minamisanriku-cho), Miyagi Prefecture, Japan.

facts.statement: Unlike more advanced ichthyosaurs, Utatsusaurus lacked a dorsal fin and possessed a broad skull.
facts.quote: Unlike the more advanced ichthyosaurs, Utatsusaurus has no dorsal fin and has a broad skull.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus was a relatively small ichthyopterygian weighing approximately 57.8 kilograms.
facts.quote: Utatsusaurus was a relatively small ichthyopterygian, measuring 2.5 - 3 m long and weighing 57.8 kg.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had a long, low tail fin, suggesting it swam by undulation rather than using paddles and a fluked tail.
facts.quote: The tail had a long low fin, suggesting that the animal swam by undulation, rather than using its paddles and tail.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had small fins with five digits, and these digits could possess up to five extra finger bones, a condition known as hyperphalangy.
facts.quote: Utatsusaurus had small fins, with five digits. In addition, those digits have up to five extra finger bones, which is referred to as hyperphalangy.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus fed on a diet of fish.
facts.quote: Utatsusaurus fed on a diet of fish.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had approximately 40 cylindrical presacral vertebrae, suggesting it swam with an eel-like motion.
facts.quote: It has approximately 40 presacral vertebrae which are cylindrical, suggesting that it probably swam with an eel-like motion.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had humeri and femurs of equal length, a trait distinct from other ichthyosaurs (longer humerus) and terrestrial amniotes (longer femur).
facts.quote: The humerus and femur of Utatsusaurus has the equal length. While all other ichthyosaurs have the longer humerus, terrestrial amniotes have the longer femur.

facts.statement: The hindlimbs of Utatsusaurus appear to be larger than its forelimbs.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the hindlimb of Utatsusaurus seems to be larger than the forelimb.

facts.statement: Ryosuke Motani, Nachio Minoura, and Tatsuro Ando re-examined Utatsusaurus fossils in 1998 using computer imagery to correct skeletal distortion.
facts.quote: Ryosuke Motani from the University of California, Berkeley, and Nachio Minoura and Tatsuro Ando from Hokkaido University re-examined the fossils of Utatsusaurus in 1998 using computer imagery to reverse the distortion of the original skeleton.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses concluded that ichthyosaurs are members of Diapsida and the sister group of Sauria.
facts.quote: They also used phylogenetic analyses and concluded that ichthyosaurs were a member of the Diapsida and the sister group of the Sauria.

facts.statement: In 2013, Cuthbertson and colleagues reported that Ichthyopterygia is a monophyletic group and Utatsusaurus forms a basal clade with Parvinatator.
facts.quote: Additionally, in 2013, Cuthbertson and colleagues from the University of Calgary, Canada, using phylogenetic analyses, reported that Ichthyopterygia is a monophyletic group and Utatsusaurus and Parvinatator are a basal clade.

facts.statement: The museum housing Utatsusaurus fossils, the Gyoryū-kan, was destroyed on March 11, 2011, during the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami.
facts.quote: However, on Friday 11 March 2011, the museum was destroyed during the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus belongs to the family Utatsusauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Utatsusauridae

facts.statement: The genus Utatsusaurus was named by Shikama, Kamei, and Murata in 1978.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Shikama, Kamei & Murata, 1978

facts.statement: The species Utatsusaurus hataii was named by Shikama, Kamei, and Murata in 1978.
facts.quote: species_authority: Shikama, Kamei & Murata, 1978

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had small teeth relative to its skull size, arranged in a primitive groove.
facts.quote: Los dientes eran pequeños para el tamaño de su cráneo, y dispuestos en un surco primitivo.

facts.statement: Detailed examination of the holotype later reported that Utatsusaurus teeth were more robust and blunt-pointed than previously thought.
facts.quote: Pero posteriormente se reportó que eran más robustos y de punta más roma tras el examen detallado del holotipo.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had a long, low tail fin, suggesting it swam by undulation rather than using paddles and a tail.
facts.quote: La cola tenía una aleta larga y baja, lo que sugiere que el animal nadaba por ondulación, en vez de usar sus aletas y su cola.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus possessed transitional features between ancestral terrestrial amniotes and more derived ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Utatsusaurus tenía rasgos transicionales entre los amniotas terrestres ancestrales y los ictiosaurios más derivados.

facts.statement: The pelvic girdle attachment in Utatsusaurus was likely not robust enough to support the body on land, unlike terrestrial amniotes.
facts.quote: En primer lugar, la sujeción de la cadera a la columna vertebral probablemente no era lo bastante robusta como para soportar al cuerpo en tierra a diferencia de los amniotas terrestres.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had humeri and femurs of equal length, whereas other ichthyosaurs had longer humeri and terrestrial amniotes had longer femurs.
facts.quote: Segundo, el húmero y el fémur de Utatsusaurus tenían igual longitud, mientras que en los demás ictiosaurios tenían un húmero más largo, y los amniotas terrestres suelen tener el fémur más largo.

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus had approximately 40 cylindrical presacral vertebrae, reinforcing the idea that it swam with an eel-like motion.
facts.quote: Poseía aproximadamente 40 vértebras presacrales que son de forma cilíndrica, lo que refuerza la idea de que nadaba con un movimiento parecido al de las anguilas.

facts.statement: Researchers found Utatsusaurus closely related to lizard-like diapsid reptiles like Petrolacosaurus, making ichthyopterygians distant relatives of lizards, snakes, and crocodiles.
facts.quote: Ellos descubrieron que Utatsusaurus estaba cercanamente relacionado con los reptiles diápsidos parecidos a lagartos como Petrolacosaurus, lo que hace a los ictiopterigios parientes distantes de los lagartos, serpientes y cocodrilos.

facts.statement: The museum displaying Utatsusaurus fossils was destroyed on March 11, 2011, by the earthquake and tsunami.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en el viernes 11 de marzo de 2011, el terremoto y tsunami de Japón de 2011 destruyeron el museo.

facts.statement: The genus Utatsusaurus was named by Shikama and Kamei in 1978.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Utatsusaurus (genus), Shikama and Kamei 1978

facts.statement: Utatsusaurus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Utatsusaurus is Utatsusaurus hataii.
facts.quote: Type species: Utatsusaurus hataii

facts.statement: A specimen assigned to cf. Utatsusaurus hataii was found in the Lower Triassic Osawa Formation in Japan.
facts.quote: A study on the anatomy of the ichthyopterygian specimen NSM-PV-20028 from the Lower Triassic Osawa Formation (Japan), assigned to cf. Utatsusaurus hataii, is published by Yoshizawa & Tsuihiji (2026).

facts.statement: Researchers Yoshizawa and Tsuihiji published a 2026 study on the anatomy of a specimen assigned to cf. Utatsusaurus hataii.
facts.quote: A study on the anatomy of the ichthyopterygian specimen NSM-PV-20028 from the Lower Triassic Osawa Formation (Japan), assigned to cf. Utatsusaurus hataii, is published by Yoshizawa & Tsuihiji (2026).

rejected.quote: The postorbital underlaps the elongate posterior process of the postfrontal. This is an evident plesiomorphic condition for ichthyopterygians.
